text: To vie is to compete with others to win something. Here, several companies are all trying to win NASA as a customer.
A habitable place is safe and comfortable enough for people to live in. Hab-1 is where astronauts will live.
A brainchild is an idea or invention that one person dreamed up and made real, as if it were born from their brain.
The private sector means businesses run by people and companies, not by the government. Here, it means a station built by a company instead of NASA.
An orbit is the curved path an object follows as it circles a planet. A station in orbit keeps falling around the Earth without ever hitting it.
A startup is a brand-new company, often trying out a bold idea.
An entrepreneur is a person who starts a new business and takes the risk that it might fail.
Here, firm is a noun meaning a company. It does not mean hard or strict, as it can in other sentences.
Aluminium is a light, silvery metal. Soda cans are made of it. This is the British spelling of aluminum.
A cylinder is a tube shape with flat round ends, like a can of soup.
Shielding is a protective layer that blocks danger, like a shield does. Here, it keeps small objects from poking through the station.
To puncture something is to poke a hole in it, like a nail in a bike tire.
Micrometeorites are tiny bits of rock, smaller than a grain of sand, zooming through space at great speed.
Debris is scattered broken pieces left over from something. Space debris is old rocket and satellite junk circling Earth.
A pressurised room has air held inside at normal pressure so people can breathe, even though space outside has no air. This is the British spelling of pressurized.
Here, volume means how much space is inside something, not how loud it is.
A cubic metre is the space inside a box one metre long, wide, and tall. Eighty of them is about the room inside a small school bus.
A docking port is a door where one spacecraft links up with another.
Microgravity is the floating feeling in orbit, where things seem to weigh almost nothing because they are falling around Earth together.
To accommodate people means to have enough room for them. This station has room for four.
A mission is a trip with a clear job to do. Each of these will last two weeks.
NASA is the United States space agency. It sends astronauts and probes into space.
ISS stands for the International Space Station, the big laboratory where astronauts live in orbit right now.
Ageing means getting old. The ISS has flown since 1998, so its parts are wearing out. This is the British spelling of aging.
To scrap something is to throw it away or end it because it is no longer useful.
Multi-module means made of many separate parts, called modules, that are joined together like building blocks.
A permanently crewed station always has people aboard, with new crews arriving as old ones leave.
Here, custom is an old word for business from customers. Companies are hoping NASA will become their customer.
An appendage is a part attached to something bigger, like an arm to a body. The service module will be attached to the ISS at first.
To detach is to come loose and separate from something it was attached to.
A service module holds the machinery that keeps a station running, such as power and air supply.
Modules are separate sections of a station that are built apart and then joined together.
Starship is SpaceX's giant next-generation rocket, built to carry far more than older rockets.
Next-generation means the newer version that comes after the current one.
Mod cons is short for modern conveniences, such as hot water, nice lighting, and comfy beds.
To plump for something means to choose it, often quickly and with confidence.
Cosy means warm, snug, and comfortable. This is the British spelling of cozy.
Trailing the field means being behind the others in a race or contest. Here, Orbital Reef is the project furthest behind.
An inflatable thing is filled with air to take shape, like a bounce house. These rooms would be packed small for launch and then blown up in space.
A spaceplane is a craft that launches like a rocket but can glide back down and land like an airplane.
A heavy-lift rocket is a very powerful rocket able to carry huge loads into space.
A controlled splashdown means steering something to land in the sea on purpose, so it does not crash onto people.
Point Nemo is the place in the Pacific Ocean farthest from any land, so falling space junk is unlikely to hurt anyone there.
To outlive something is to last longer than expected. The ISS has survived three earlier plans to end it.
Haven-1 is the first small station built by the company Vast. It is meant to be a test before a bigger one.
Airbus is a large European company that builds airplanes and spacecraft.
SpaceX is the private company that launches rockets and carries astronauts, using rockets that can land and be reused.
Blue Origin is a private rocket company started by Jeff Bezos, who also founded Amazon.
Falcon 9 is a SpaceX rocket, the one most often used to launch satellites and astronauts today.
